chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

Abu Baseer asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I was present. So he said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Should I recite the Quran in one night?' So he said: 'No'. So he said, 'In two nights?' So he said: 'No'. Until it reached six nights. So he gestured by his hand, and said: 'Ha!'

Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! The ones who were before you from the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) used to recite the Quran in a month, and less. The Quran is such that it should not be recited by jabbering, but slowly and with clarity. Whenever you pass by a Verse wherein is a Mention of the Fire, pause at it and seek Refuge with Allah from the Fire'.

So Abu Baseer said, 'Should I recite the Quran in one night of the Month of Ramazan?' So he said: 'No'. So he said, 'In two nights?' So he said: 'No'. So he said, 'In three?' So he said: 'Ha!', and gestured by his hand, 'Yes, the Month of Ramazan is such that nothing resembles it from the (other) months. For it is a right and a sanctity. Frequent from the Salat, whatever your capacity may be'.

key_terms.تَرْتِيلًا: Reciting slowly and clearly with proper pronunciation

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended time to complete reciting the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the Companions of the Prophet (PBUH) typically completed the Quran in a month, rushing through it is discouraged in favor of *tartil* (measured, reflective recitation), pausing at verses of warning or promise. The hadith further elevates Ramadan as a unique month with distinct spiritual rights, linking the completion of Quran recitation to increased devotion and prayer, thereby establishing a balanced approach between speed and contemplation.

en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamza who has said the following: “Once, abu Basil’ asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) when I was also present, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, can I read the Holy Quran in one night?’ The Imam said, ‘No.’ He then asked, ‘Can I read it in two nights?’ The Imam said, ‘No,’ until he reached six nights, the Imam (a.s.) made a hand gesture saying ‘Ha’ a,’ (a hint for approval).

Then the Imam (a.s.) said, ‘O abu Muhammad, note that among the companions of Muhammad (a.s.) before you, there were those who would read the Holy Quran once in a month or less. The Holy Quran is not read in a big rush but it is read with proper elocution and distinct pronunciation. When you come across a verse that speaks of the fire you pause and ask Allah for protection.’

Abu Basir then asked, ‘Can I read the Holy Quran in the month of Ramadan once every night?’ The Imam said, ‘No.’ He then asked, ‘Can I read it in two nights?’ The Imam said, ‘No.’ He then asked, ‘Can I read it in three nights?’ The Imam said, ‘Ha’ a, ’ with a hand gesture for approval saying, ‘Yes, the month of Ramadan is not like the other months. It has its rights and respect. Increase in prayer as much as you can.’”
